clue.text: Providing fleet around to restore calm

indicators.note: around tells us the word for fleet goes round the word for providing

parts.note: fleet as an adjective means fast or swift, and pacy is a British word for quick
providing that means on condition that, the same as the conditional if

explanation.surface: Someone hopes a naval fleet sailing around will bring calm back to troubled waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' tempts as a navy sailing round, but it is the adjective meaning quick; 'around' is the container signal and 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify is to soothe or quieten, which is bringing back a peaceful state.

clue.text: European character going to parts of Germany to have affairs

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, Greece being in Europe
the Länder are the federal states of Germany

explanation.surface: A Greek letter makes its way to German regions in search of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to have casual love affairs, especially as a man.

clue.text: Exclusive group in poet's small house on lake

parts.note: cot is a poetic word for a cottage
Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A select circle gathers in a poet's lakeside cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'on' are link words; in a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small close circle of people with shared interests.

clue.text: Ceremony outside university meeting place

indicators.note: outside says the ceremony word goes round the university letter

parts.note: a form is a set ritual or ceremony

explanation.surface: A ritual is held outside a campus assembly hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum was the public square of a Roman town where people gathered.

clue.text: Substitute needed by second minute to cover a sudden attack

indicators.note: to cover says the stand-in word wraps around the little word a

parts.note: a proxy is someone who stands in or acts as a substitute
S is the standard abbreviation for a second of time
M is the standard abbreviation for a minute of time

explanation.surface: A stand-in is rushed in with seconds to spare to cover for a sudden assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed by' simply joins the pieces; 'to cover' has PROXY wrap A, giving PAROXY.
explanation.definitionFit: A paroxysm is a sudden violent outburst or fit, as of coughing or rage.

clue.text: Subconscious mechanism used by American car salesman?

definitions.meaning: self-induced influence on one's own mind, below conscious thought
an auto is an American car, so a salesman's pitch would be a car suggestion

explanation.definitionFit: The psychological term for self-hypnotic influence also reads as a tip about a motor vehicle.

clue.text: Team of players looking to score

definitions.text: Team of players looking to score

parts.words: Team of players looking to score
parts.note: sounds like a sports side hoping for a goal, but means musicians reading a written score

explanation.definitionFit: A large group of instrumentalists plays from a printed musical score.

clue.text: Quantity of cloth to put over, for instance, a cart

indicators.note: to put over in a down clue means the string is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: eg, exempli gratia, means for instance
a dray is a low cart for heavy loads, such as beer barrels

explanation.surface: A measure of fabric is draped over a cart, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put over' reverses EG + A + DRAY as one string.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is an amount measured in yards, as of fabric.

clue.text: Aimlessly loiter in 'second old church

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second, as in 'half a mo'

explanation.surface: Someone hangs around idly in an old church for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch is to wander about without purpose.

clue.text: Inlet could possibly be lost Nile branch

indicators.note: could possibly be suggests the letters of lost nile branch might be rearranged into another phrase

explanation.surface: Perhaps an inlet is really a lost arm of the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bristol Channel is the wide sea arm between south Wales and south-west England.

clue.text: Reprint badly backed note to make wording clear

indicators.note: badly tells us the letters of the word reprint are put together wrongly, in a new order
backed means the musical note is turned round so it reads from the back

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, also spelt ti

explanation.surface: A garbled reprint gets a note on the back explaining what the text means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' shuffles REPRINT into INTERPR; 'backed' turns TE into ET.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret a text is to explain its meaning so that it can be understood.

clue.text: Goods being moved 'about old ship

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about, used with approximate dates
the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek legend

explanation.surface: Merchandise is shifted around an old vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goods being moved' looks like wordplay of motion, but it is the definition; 'about' is C.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight carried by a ship or plane is goods in transit.

clue.text: Notice rapid eye-movement in disturbing dream? That's relevant

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a public notice
REM is the usual abbreviation for rapid eye movement, the dreaming stage of sleep

explanation.surface: Someone spots the twitching eyes of a person in a troubled dream and calls it significant.
explanation.walkthrough: A bonus: 'in disturbing dream' is also an anagram (signalled by 'disturbing') of DREAM, giving the same letters, so the clue offers two routes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad rem is Latin for 'to the thing', meaning pertinent to the matter in hand.

clue.text: English crack regiment beats back last of French

parts.note: the SAS, the Special Air Service, is the British army's elite regiment

indicators.note: back means the word for beats is reversed

parts.note: to cane someone is to beat them, so canes means beats

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word French

explanation.surface: An elite English regiment drives back the French rearguard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses CANES to SENAC. SASSENACH is the Scots (often derogatory) word for an English person, so 'English' is a fair if sly definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots and Irish speakers use the word as a term for an Englishman or English person.

clue.text: Lack of water outside Aden for manoeuvring warship

indicators.note: outside says the dry-spell word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a drought is a long spell without rain

indicators.note: manoeuvring tells us the letters of Aden are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A warship manoeuvres off the port of Aden despite a shortage of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; 'manoeuvring' rearranges the port's four letters, and 'outside' wraps the dry-spell word around them.
explanation.definitionFit: The dreadnought was a type of early 20th-century battleship named after HMS Dreadnought.

clue.text: One who thought of French actress improperly.

parts.note: de is the French word for of

indicators.note: improperly means the letters of actress are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A man who fantasised indecently about a French actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improperly' turns ACTRESS into SCARTES. 'One who thought' nods at 'I think, therefore I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: René Descartes was the French philosopher famous for 'cogito ergo sum'.

clue.text: What can reveal some pebbles?

indicators.note: some means only part of the word pebbles is taken, the letters inside it

explanation.surface: A riddle about what uncovers stones on a beach.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a receding tide uncovers pebbles on the shore, and 'some pebbles' holds the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: When the tide goes out it exposes stones and sand that the sea had covered.

clue.text: Plant, say, in black bowl

indicators.note: in tells us the word for say goes inside the other letters

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a cup is a small bowl-shaped vessel
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A plant, for example, sits in a black bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is a verb here; 'in' sets it between the colour letter and the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow-flowered meadow plant.

clue.text: Hit song

definitions.meaning: to strike sharply, as on a door
a piece of rhythmic spoken music

explanation.definitionFit: Rap means both a sharp knock and a spoken-word style of popular music.

clue.text: Ancient city preserved ceremony, one that's taken up here

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial splendour

indicators.note: taken up in a down clue means the letters are lifted, read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: An ancient city kept a rite alive, one taken up there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' reverses I + IE to EII. 'here' is a link pointing to the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was the Roman town buried and so kept intact by Vesuvius's ash in AD 79.

clue.text: Create a stir in order to reform government department

indicators.note: reform means the letters of create a stir are formed again into a different word

explanation.surface: Someone stirs things up so as to shake up a ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order to' is link material; 'reform' rearranges the eleven letters of CREATE A STIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretariat is the administrative office of a government or organisation.

clue.text: Is cooler needed around a hot Iranian city?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: around says the fan word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a fan cools the air
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Does a hot Iranian city need a fan running?
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts A + H inside FAN, giving FAHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Isfahan (Esfahan) is a historic city in central Iran.

clue.text: Soldier?

parts.note: read as a fighter it is a plain synonym; the question mark hints at the soldier ant, an insect caste that fights

explanation.definitionFit: A fighter in war is a combatant, and a soldier ant is the fighting ant of its colony.

clue.text: Low bird cry is heard

indicators.note: is heard means the word for the bird call is spoken and sounds like the answer

parts.note: a cheep is the shrill cry of a young bird

explanation.surface: A bird's faint call can be made out.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap and low both describe something inexpensive or base.

clue.text: Writer rejected English coming from editor

indicators.note: rejected means the whole string is thrown back, read in reverse

parts.note: of means coming from, as in a man of Kent

explanation.surface: An author turns down English copy sent by an editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses E + OF + ED, giving the novelist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the English author of Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: Suitable wear, affected by heat in Indian interior

indicators.note: in places the heat word inside the letters taken from the middle
interior picks the central letters of the word Indian

parts.note: something affected by heat has become hot

explanation.surface: Clothing appropriate for the heat in inland India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interior' takes the middle two letters of the six-letter word, and 'in' places the heat word between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The dhoti is the loose loincloth worn by Hindu men, suited to a hot climate.

clue.text: Throw out unacceptable article that's not right

indicators.note: that's not means the following letter is taken away from the item

parts.note: a reject is a manufactured item not good enough to sell

explanation.surface: Discard a substandard item that isn't correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's not right' removes R from REJECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject is to expel or force out.

clue.text: Like some 18th century buildings, gone rotten, old and mostly dull

indicators.note: rotten tells us the letters of gone are spoilt into a new order
mostly means the last letter of the word for dull is dropped

parts.note: thick means dull or stupid

explanation.surface: Some Georgian buildings have decayed, aged and become drab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' turns GONE into NEOG; 'mostly' trims THICK to THIC. Gothic Revival began in the 18th century, at Strawberry Hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Neo-Gothic describes revival architecture imitating medieval styles, popular from the 1700s.

clue.text: Trader's line in footwear

definitions.meaning: the ... line is the load mark painted on a merchant ship's hull
light canvas sports shoes with rubber soles

explanation.walkthrough: A merchant ship is a 'trader'. 'in' is a link. Plimsolls are the British name for canvas sneakers.
explanation.definitionFit: The load line on merchant vessels and the canvas gym shoe share the same name.

clue.text: Pinch child's skin to keep awake? The opposite

parts.note: kid is the soft leather of a young goat, a kid being a child too
the opposite of staying awake is to doze, to nap

explanation.surface: Squeezing a youngster's cheek to stop them nodding off, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinch' looks like a squeeze but is slang for steal, here a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinch is slang for steal, and kidnapping is stealing a person.
